class.name: BlenderConstraint3D
class.brief_description: A Blender bone or object constraint, evaluated with Blender's own math.
class.description: [BlenderConstraint3D] acts like one constraint in Blender's constraint stack. Its owner is a bone of the parent [Skeleton3D] or, when [member owner_node] is set, another [Node3D] such as a prop that follows a hand. Its target is a bone of the same skeleton or any [Node3D]. The constraint is evaluated the way Blender evaluates it: in the owner and target spaces Blender offers, with Blender's mix modes, Euler rotation orders, offsets, limits and influence. Settings use the names they have in Blender's Python API, such as [code]use_offset[/code] or [code]mix_mode[/code], and appear in the Inspector under the constraint type's settings. Use [method set_setting] and [method get_setting] to change them from a script. Coordinates follow a [Skeleton3D] imported from Blender: its armature space is Blender's armature space turned from Z up to Y up, with the bones' own axes kept. Limits, offsets and matrices are in Blender's axes. Importing a [code].blend[/code] file with [b]Blender > Rigs > Rebuild Constraints[/b] on adds one [BlenderConstraint3D] for each Copy Location, Copy Rotation, Copy Scale, Copy Transforms, Limit Location, Limit Rotation, Limit Scale, Child Of, Damped Track, Track To, Locked Track, Stretch To, Transformation and Maintain Volume constraint, in the order Blender evaluates them. The import mutes the constraints it rebuilds exactly, so the imported animations carry the poses before them and each constraint acts once, here. A constraint that stays baked into the animation, for example one whose influence is animated, is added switched off with [member SkeletonModifier3D.active], and the import says why. Several [BlenderConstraint3D] nodes on one bone act in their order under the [Skeleton3D], as a stack does in Blender. For a bone owner, the skeleton blends the result by [member SkeletonModifier3D.influence]; for a node owner, the constraint blends it.

method.name: get_setting
method.description: Returns the setting with Blender's name [param name], such as [code]"use_offset"[/code], or its default if it was never set.

method.name: get_settings
method.description: Returns every setting of the [member constraint_type], by Blender's names, with their current values.

method.name: needs_target
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the [member constraint_type] reads a target. Limit Location, Limit Rotation, Limit Scale and Maintain Volume don't.

method.name: set_setting
method.description: Sets the setting with Blender's name [param name]. Enumerations take Blender's identifiers as strings, such as [code]"TRACK_NEGATIVE_Z"[/code]; angles are in radians.

method.name: set_settings
method.description: Replaces all settings with [param settings], by Blender's names. Settings left out take their defaults.

members.member: The index of the owner bone.
The name of the owner bone. Not used when [member owner_node] is set.
The Blender constraint this node evaluates. Each type has its own settings.
Where along the target bone the target is, from its head ([code]0.0[/code]) to its tail ([code]1.0[/code]), as Blender's [b]Head/Tail[/b].
A [Node3D] that this constraint moves instead of a bone, as an object constraint does in Blender. The node's own transform is the constraint's input, and its world transform the output.
The Euler rotation order of the owner in Blender, which settings set to [code]"AUTO"[/code] use. A quaternion or axis-angle owner uses [code]"XYZ"[/code], as in Blender.
The space the owner is evaluated in. A node owner uses [constant SPACE_WORLD].
The length of the target bone in Blender, which [member head_tail] measures along.
The target bone, in the same [Skeleton3D]. Takes precedence over [member target_node].
A [Node3D] target, as an object target in Blender.
The Euler rotation order of the target in Blender, which Child Of uses when it copies some rotation axes only.
The space the target is read in. A node target uses [constant SPACE_WORLD].

constants.constant: Copies the target's location, per axis, with offset and inversion.
Copies the target's rotation as Euler angles, per axis, with Blender's mix modes.
Copies the target's scale, per axis or uniformly, with power and offset.
Copies the target's whole transform, or combines it with the owner's by a mix mode.
Holds the owner's location within limits.
Holds the owner's Euler angles within limits.
Holds the owner's scale within limits.
Moves the owner with the target as a child does with its parent, using the inverse matrix Blender set.
Turns one axis of the owner toward the target by the least turn.
Points one axis of the owner at the target, keeping another axis up.
Points one axis of the owner toward the target, turning only about a locked axis.
Points the owner's Y axis at the target and stretches it to reach, with volume preservation.
Maps a range of the target's location, rotation or scale to a range of the owner's.
Scales the owner's other axes to keep its volume as one axis scales.
Represents the size of the [enum ConstraintType] enum.
Blender's Pose Space: the armature's space.
Blender's Local With Parent space: relative to the bone's rest pose in the armature.
Blender's Local Space: relative to the bone's rest pose under its posed parent.
